environment.note: Replication is CPU-only Octave work; the GPU is irrelevant to this MATLAB codebase. Code run under Octave 6.4.0 via the shipped compat layer (octave_port.patch + shims/). No MATLAB license needed.
environment.graphics_stack: gnuplot 6.0.5 (installed via micromamba, no root); Octave ft-font renderer fixed with an LD_PRELOAD interposer redirecting the compiled-in missing FreeSans path to DejaVu; a ghostscript-based drop-in epstool for tight EPS bounding boxes.

paper: Hsieh, Hurst, Jones & Klenow, 'The Allocation of Talent and U.S. Economic Growth', Econometrica 87(5), 2019
data: chad_output_file_2019_01_24.csv (8040 rows x 14 cols), the aggregated model-input CSV (not the large .dta microdata).
pipeline_per_case: SetParameters -> ReadCohortData -> EstimateTauZ_main -> CleanandShowTauAZ -> SolveEqmBasic -> HowMuchPoorer
known_limitations: theta is calibrated to 2 in SetParameters; the MLE of theta*(1-eta) (paper reports ~1.24-1.42) is NOT shipped in the provided code, so that structural estimate was not reproduced (no code path exists for it).

Step 3 supplementary figures BlauKahn.eps and CharlesGuryan.eps (not in the plan's figure list) were not produced due to a known Octave gnuplot-toolkit hang on labeled scatter plots; all plan-required Fig1-Fig7 were produced.
Step 4 scatter figures (estimatedeltaYWM_*) not written: those runs used the no-op print shim to guarantee numeric completion; the numeric delta estimates fully reproduce.

Step 8 opening fact has no shipped script; reconstructed with an all-cohort, population-weighted convention. 1960 matches the paper's 94% exactly; 2010 is 57.7% vs the paper's ~62% (aggregation-convention difference, reported faithfully, not tuned).
suspicions: none (suspicions.json = []); the shipped code reproduces all plan claims faithfully.
